Modeled from its README's 'Core Concepts' section: a Receipt is an append-only BLAKE3-chained log of Events, each carrying a Commitment (a BLAKE3 digest of payload data -- payloads themselves are never stored in the receipt). Every CertifyStage/Command triple was hand-verified 2026-07-18 against the actual ~/affidavit README.md on disk (byte-for-byte match, not just 'plausible from prose'), version-pinned via afd:sourceVersion in ontology.ttl. No command-surface enumeration attempted for the other 55 verbs (the README documents 59 canonical verbs total in prose only, no table); this pack covers the receipt data model plus 4 named core verbs, not the full CLI. Generates: (1) src/affidavit_catalog.rs -- reference tables (CERTIFY_STAGES, CORE_VERBS); (2) src/affidavit_certify.rs -- real executable logic: an ontology-order-derived Stage dispatcher (next_stage/is_terminal), plus (round 3, 2026-07-18) two generic domain-independent structural primitives (check_strictly_increasing/check_unique) composed by check_stage() per-stage from the ontology's afd:checksMonotonic/afd:checksUnique boolean facts -- check_continuity() is now a thin named call into that ontology-driven dispatch rather than one hand-written affidavit-specific body, proven against adversarial duplicate/out-of-order inputs plus the composition/dispatch mechanism itself in tests/affidavit_certify_proof.rs; (3) docs/affidavit_reference.md; (4) src/affidavit_lib_wiring.rs (force:true, plain file -- NOT inject-mode; retargeted off src/lib.rs during round 2's cross-pack verification after two other packs collided writing to that same path in a shared consumer) containing `pub mod affidavit_catalog;`/`pub mod affidavit_certify;`, which the consumer must mount with one `include!("affidavit_lib_wiring.rs");` line in their own src/lib.rs -- a disclosed, real remaining consumer-effort step, not 'wires ggen.toml, done'. Both affidavit_catalog.rs/affidavit_certify.rs use freeze_policy=checksum (freeze_slots_dir=.ggen/freeze/affidavit-pack) so a hand-edit to generated output is detected and regeneration is skipped rather than silently clobbered.

Round 4 (2026-07-19, real reference found at ~/affidavit -- the actual crate checkout on this machine, not merely its README): the prior rounds above modeled only the CertifyStage labels/order/rejectCondition prose. This round transcribes ~/affidavit's actual `src/types.rs`/`src/chain.rs`/`src/verifier.rs` (v26.6.22, checksummed copies committed read-only at `reference/affidavit_v26.6.22_src/{types,chain,verifier}.rs` -- `shasum -a 256` confirmed byte-identical against the live `~/affidavit/src/*.rs` at copy time) into three new generated modules: `src/affidavit_types.rs` (Blake3Hash/ObjectRef/OperationEvent/Receipt with its forgery-resistant custom Deserialize/CheckOutcome/Verdict/ProfileId/canonical_bytes -- the `Evidence<_,Admitted,_>`/wasm4pm_compat witness-type layer is deliberately NOT transcribed, out of this pack's ontology scope), `src/affidavit_chain.rs` (real BLAKE3 rolling-chain-hash ChainAssembler/recompute_chain/content_address/serialize_receipt/deserialize_receipt, byte-for-byte port of the real algorithm, not a paraphrase), `src/affidavit_verifier.rs` (the real 6-function stage_decode/stage_check_format/stage_chain_integrity/stage_continuity/stage_verify_commitments/stage_evaluate_profile + verify() dispatch, identical control flow to the reference). Reusable manufacturing capital for isolating a parallel multi-agent fleet
across a repo tree. Makes `ggen sync run` refuse (FM-PACK-013) when a fleet
plan declares two agents sharing a worktree or a build-cache directory, when
an agent never emitted a cwd-assertion proving it actually ran in its
assigned worktree, or when an agent raised a jidoka stop that was never
resolved. Closes the failure mode named in the 2026-09-02 Claude Code
insights report's "On the Horizon" section: agents colliding on a shared
working tree or build cache, or a verify subagent running in the wrong cwd
and reporting false findings.

Consumer contract: declare the fleet plan (fleet:Agent individuals with
assignedRepo/worktreePath/buildCacheDir) in your own ontology source, wire
this pack in [packs], run the generated scripts/fleet-manifest.sh to create
the worktrees, dispatch agents with scripts/agent-preamble.sh as their
mandatory first action (it appends a real fleet:CwdAssertion fact to
evidence/ontology.ttl), then `ggen sync run`. A worktree/build-cache
collision, a missing or mismatched cwd assertion, or an unresolved
fleet:JidokaStop each refuse sync -- the fleet cannot be reported done while
any of these hold.

No external ontology is unioned — this pack's vocabulary is self-contained PROV/DCMI/SKOS/OWL-Time, so no ggen.toml extra_ontologies entry is required. require another pack be present. This pack's vocabulary/gate is therefore not "depended on" by
any consumer of a second projection-target pack (e.g. packs/shacl-to-pydantic-pack) in any

Projects the standard Supabase client/config wiring for any Node.js project

@supabase/supabase-js 2.38-2.108 (Next.js apps, Nuxt apps, Expo/React Native apps, and plain
Node backends). Two findings from that mining shaped the pack's default:

1. The dominant real client pattern is a single-instance `createClient()` call in a small

   `@supabase/ssr` cookie-based dual client/server pattern -- `@supabase/ssr` showed up only

   `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` had zero real usage anywhere scanned. This pack therefore

   client; `@supabase/ssr` dual client/server generation is available opt-in per `sb:Client`
   when `runtime` is set to "server" or "edge" alongside `package = "@supabase/ssr"`, for
   projects that do want Next.js App Router SSR auth.

2. Real environment variable names split by target: Node/backend projects overwhelmingly use
   bare `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` / `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`; Expo/React Native
   projects use the `EXPO_PUBLIC_` prefix required for Expo's public env var convention; a
   smaller minority of Next.js projects use `NEXT_PUBLIC_`. This pack projects the env var
   prefix from `sb:Client.runtime` and an explicit `sb:Project.envPrefix` fact rather than
   assuming one framework's convention project-wide.
